title: Diamond Graph Push-Pull Evaluation
description: Trace how a single write to Signal A propagates Dirty and Check marks before Effect D lazily evaluates once with consistent values.

steps.label: 1. Initial Clean Graph
steps.description: All four nodes are synchronized. Source A holds 1; derived nodes B (A * 2) and C (A + 1) hold 2; sink D (B + C) holds 4 with 1 total execution.
steps.codeHighlight: const A = signal(1); const B = computed(() => A() * 2); const C = computed(() => A() + 1); const D = effect(() => B() + C());

steps.label: 2. Push Phase: Write A = 2
steps.description: A increments its version and pushes invalidation marks without running user code. Direct dependents B and C become Dirty; transitive sink D becomes Check.
steps.codeHighlight: A.set(2); // marks B, C -> Dirty; marks D -> Check

steps.label: 3. Pull Phase: D Verifies B First
steps.description: Effect D flushes. Because D is marked Check, it defers its own body and pulls upstream dependency B first. B recomputes 2 * 2 = 4 and marks D Dirty.
steps.codeHighlight: updateIfNecessary(B); // B: 2 -> 4, flips D from Check to Dirty

steps.label: 4. Pull Phase: D Reads C
steps.description: D begins evaluating B() + C(). B() returns cached 4 immediately; C() triggers updateIfNecessary(C), which computes 2 + 1 = 3 before returning to D.

steps.label: 5. Consistent Commit (Zero Glitches)
steps.description: D completes with B = 4 and C = 3, committing 7 and resetting to Clean. D never observed the torn state (B = 4, C = 2) and ran exactly once for this write.
